mainTopic: Which features count as a סימן for lost items: knots, number, weight, cuts, seals, location, and recognition by sight
overview: The גמרא keeps going through the משנה's list of found items the finder may keep, such as strings of fish and cuts of meat. Each time, it asks why a knot, a number or a weight does not count as a סימן. The answer each time is that in these cases everyone's items look the same. Along the way, רב ששת proves from a ברייתא that weight, and therefore number and measure too, can be a סימן. A cut of meat counts only if it has a special shape, not because of the body part it came from. Next the גמרא resolves a contradiction between barrels the finder keeps and jugs he must announce. One answer is sealed versus covered containers. אביי's answer is before versus after the wine storehouses open. The גמרא then asks whether the place an item was found counts as a סימן, and works through proofs and a story about pitch found near a winepress. Finally it explains the משנה's word אנפוריא as new vessels, which matters for a צורבא מרבנן who claims an item by recognizing it on sight.

steps.title: Why isn't the knot on a string of fish a sign?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of strings of fish and asks why the knot does not count as a סימן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says strings of fish belong to the finder. Why? The knot should be a סימן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה, strings of fish, and challenges it. If the knot could identify the owner, the finder should have to announce the find.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An item with a סימן must be announced so the owner can claim it. A knot looks like a possible סימן, so the משנה's ruling that the finder keeps the fish seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Strings (fish threaded together on a cord)
An identifying mark that lets the owner prove the item is his

phrases.english: And strings of fish.
Why? Let the knot be a sign!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the line-by-line analysis of the משנה's list of items the finder may keep.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that strings of fish belong to the finder.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A knot could be distinctive, which would make it a סימן and require announcing the find.

steps.title: It is the standard fisherman's knot
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means a regular fisherman's knot that everyone ties, so it identifies no one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is talking about a fisherman's knot, which everyone ties the same way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the knot in the משנה is the ordinary knot that all fishermen use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סימן only works if it is special to one owner. A knot that everybody ties cannot point to any particular person, so the finder keeps the fish.

phrases.english: With a fisherman's knot,
which everyone ties this way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the knot.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any knot could identify the owner.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means a common knot that everyone uses, so it is not a סימן.

steps.title: Why isn't the number of fish a sign?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: the number of fish on the string should serve as a סימן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the number of fish on the string be a סימן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge. Even if the knot is ordinary, the owner could say how many fish were on the string.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This challenge assumes that a number can count as a סימן. If it can, the finder should have to announce the string of fish.

phrases.english: And let the number be a sign!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to the same משנה after the first was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling about strings of fish.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The count of fish could identify the owner.

steps.title: Every string has the same number
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means strings that all hold the same number of fish, so the number tells nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is talking about a number that is the same on every string.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that in this case every string of fish has the same count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the knot, a number only identifies the owner if it is unusual. When all strings hold the same number, the count proves nothing.

phrases.english: With a number that is the same for all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the number.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The count of fish would identify the owner.
steps.terutzMaskana: Every string holds the same count, so the number is not a סימן here.
steps.whatToRemember: A knot or a number is only a סימן when it is special to the owner. Something everyone shares cannot identify anyone.

steps.title: Is a number a sign? A question to רב ששת
steps.stepSummary: The scholars ask רב ששת whether a number counts as a סימן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רב ששת: is a number a סימן or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The previous step assumed a number could be a סימן. Now the scholars ask רב ששת directly whether that is true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A number might be too common or easy to guess to really prove ownership. That is why it is a real question whether it counts as a סימן.

phrases.english: They asked Rav Sheshet:

phrases.aramaic: [מִנְיָן] הָוֵי סִימָן אוֹ לָא הָוֵי סִימָן?
phrases.english: Is a number a sign, or is it not a sign?
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording; some versions don't have it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks directly about the idea that steps 3-4 assumed, that a number can be a סימן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the number of items counts as a valid סימן.

steps.title: רב ששת proves from weight that number is a sign
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת quotes a ברייתא in which giving the correct weight is enough to get back metal vessels. If weight is a סימן, then measure and number are too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: You already learned it. A ברייתא says that if someone finds silver vessels, copper vessels, lead pieces, or any metal vessels, he does not return them until the claimant gives a sign or gives the exact weight. Since weight counts as a סימן, measure and number count too.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers from a ברייתא that weight is a סימן. From this he concludes that measure and number are also סימנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lets an owner prove ownership with the exact weight alone. Weight, measure and number are all kinds of amount, so רב ששת treats them the same. The answer is yes, a number is a סימן.

keyTerms.meaning: You already learned it (in a ברייתא)
A broken piece of a vessel

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב ששת, weight, measure and number all count as a סימן.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said to them: You learned it:
If he found silver vessels and copper vessels,

phrases.aramaic: גִּסְטְרוֹן שֶׁל אֲבָר, וְכׇל כְּלֵי מַתָּכוֹת –
phrases.english: a piece of lead, or any metal vessels,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יַחֲזִיר עַד שֶׁיִּתֵּן אוֹת,
phrases.english: he does not return them until the claimant gives a sign,
or until he states their weight exactly.
And since weight is a sign,
measure and number are also a sign.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question put to רב ששת.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. A number is a סימן, learned from the ברייתא that treats weight as a סימן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about found metal vessels returned when the owner gives their exact weight.

steps.title: Why isn't the weight of the meat a sign?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of cuts of meat and asks why their weight does not count as a סימן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says cuts of meat belong to the finder. Why? The weight should be a סימן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה, cuts of meat. Using what רב ששת just proved, it asks why the weight is not a סימן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that weight is a סימן. So a cut of meat with a known weight should have to be announced, yet the משנה lets the finder keep it.

phrases.english: And cuts of meat, etc.
Why? Let the weight be a sign!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה and uses רב ששת's rule to challenge the next case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that cuts of meat belong to the finder.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Weight is a סימן, as רב ששת proved, so the meat should have to be announced.

steps.title: All the cuts weigh the same
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means cuts that all weigh the same, so the weight identifies nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is talking about a weight that is the same for all cuts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same kind of answer it gave about the number of fish: in this case every cut has the same weight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Weight is normally a סימן, but not when every piece weighs the same. Then it cannot point to one owner.

keyTerms.meaning: With a weight that is the same for all

phrases.english: With a weight that is the same for all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about weight.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The weight of the meat identifies the owner.
steps.terutzMaskana: All the cuts weigh the same, so the weight is not a סימן here.

steps.title: The cut itself should be a sign, as a ברייתא shows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges that the cut itself, whether from the neck or the thigh, should be a סימן. It supports this with a ברייתא that requires announcing found pieces of fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the cut itself be a סימן: whether it is from the neck or from the thigh! Isn't it taught in a ברייתא: if someone finds pieces of fish or a bitten fish, he must announce it. But barrels of wine, oil, grain, dried figs or olives belong to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another challenge: the body part the meat came from should identify it. It brings a ברייתא where pieces of fish must be announced, which seems to show that the cut itself is a סימן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא puts pieces of fish in the 'must announce' group, unlike plain barrels of food. The גמרא understands that the סימן there is which part of the fish the piece came from. If so, a cut of meat should also be a סימן because of which part of the animal it came from.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it taught in a ברייתא?

phrases.english: But let the cut itself be a sign,
whether it is from the neck or from the thigh!
Isn't it taught in a baraita:
If he found pieces of fish or a bitten fish,
he is obligated to announce it.
Barrels of wine or of oil,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל תְּבוּאָה וְשֶׁל גְּרוֹגְרוֹת וְשֶׁל זֵיתִים –
phrases.english: or of grain, or of dried figs, or of olives,
these belong to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge on the same משנה after the weight question was answered, now backed by a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that cuts of meat belong to the finder.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires announcing pieces of fish, seemingly because the body part is a סימן, and the same should apply to meat.

steps.title: The ברייתא means a cut with a special shape
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is about a cut with a special shape, like the three-cornered cuts of רבה בר רב הונא, not about the body part.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case is the ברייתא talking about? When there is a סימן in the way it was cut, like רבה בר רב הונא, who used to cut his meat into three-cornered pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's pieces of fish are identified by an unusual cutting shape, not by which part of the fish they came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The body part does not identify an owner, since many people have pieces from the same part. A special cutting style, like רבה בר רב הונא's triangles, does. So the ברייתא does not contradict the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
The cut, the way it was sliced

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the body part (neck or thigh) is the סימן. The סימן is the special shape of the cut.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Where there is a sign in the cut,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: like that of Rabba bar Rav Huna,
who would cut it with three corners.
phrases.notes: Meaning triangle-shaped pieces; that unusual shape is the identifying mark.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא treats the body part of the fish as a סימן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a special cutting shape. The body part alone is not a סימן.

steps.title: The ברייתא's wording supports this answer
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists pieces of fish right next to a bitten fish, which has a visible mark. This shows the pieces also have a visible mark, the shape of the cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also exact: the ברייתא puts it next to a bitten fish. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its answer from how the ברייתא is written and closes with שמע מינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bitten fish is identified by a visible mark, the bite. Since the pieces of fish are listed alongside it, they too must be identified by a visible mark, the shape of the cut. This confirms the answer in step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also exact (and supports this)
Learn from it: the point is proven

steps.whatToRemember: A cut of meat or fish is a סימן only if it has a special shape. Which part of the animal it came from does not count.

phrases.english: The wording is also exact, since it teaches it
alongside a bitten fish.
Learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּיְקָא נָמֵי דְּקָתָנֵי דּוּמְיָא דְּדָג נָשׁוּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 10 from the ברייתא's wording.
steps.raayaObject: That the סימן in the ברייתא is a visible mark, the shape of the cut.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא lists pieces of fish together with a bitten fish, whose bite is a visible mark.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The shape of the cut is a סימן. The body part it came from is not.

steps.title: Barrels belong to the finder, but jugs must be announced?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's rule that found barrels of wine, oil, grain, dried figs, or olives belong to the finder. It then challenges it from a משנה that requires announcing found jugs of wine or oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: barrels of wine, oil, grain, dried figs, or olives belong to the finder. But didn't we learn in a משנה that for jugs of wine or oil, he must announce them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line from the ברייתא and points out that a משנה seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lets the finder keep barrels of wine and oil. The משנה requires announcing jugs of wine and oil. These look like the same kind of item with opposite rulings, so the גמרא needs a way to tell the cases apart.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Master said": the formula for quoting a line from a source cited earlier
To announce a found item so its owner can claim it

phrases.english: The Master said: barrels of wine
phrases.notes: "The Master" here means the ברייתא the גמרא has been quoting.

phrases.english: or of oil, or of grain
or of dried figs, or of olives
these belong to him.
But didn't we learn in a משנה:
jugs of wine or jugs of oil
he is obligated to announce!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line in the same ברייתא that was discussed in steps 9-11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that found barrels of wine and oil belong to the finder
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה requires announcing jugs of wine and oil, which seems to be the same case with the opposite ruling.

steps.title: The משנה is about sealed jugs
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא in the name of רב answers that the משנה is about jugs with a seal, and the seal works as a סימן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רב: our משנה is talking about sealed jugs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying the משנה is about a special case: sealed jugs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each owner seals his containers in his own way, so a seal can identify him. That is why the משנה requires an announcement. The ברייתא, which lets the finder keep them, must be about containers without such a seal.

keyTerms.meaning: Marked or sealed with the owner's own seal

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said in the name of Rav:
Our משנה is about sealed jugs.
phrases.notes: Literally "marked": each person seals his jugs in his own way, so the seal can show who owns it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (sealed vs. not sealed)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא are about the same kind of container.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about sealed jugs, which carry a סימן. The ברייתא is about barrels without one.

steps.title: Open barrels would be a loss on purpose
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה is about sealed jugs, then the ברייתא must be about open barrels. But leaving a barrel open is an אבידה מדעת, so that would be too obvious to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies the ברייתא is about open barrels. But if they are open, that is a loss the owner caused on purpose!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 13 by looking at what it implies about the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine in an open barrel will spoil, so whoever left it open has given it up himself. Of course the finder may keep it. A ברייתא would not need to teach something that obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication, from what was just said
A loss the owner caused knowingly, which the finder need not return

phrases.english: This implies that the ברייתא is about open barrels
but if they are open, it is a loss on purpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what step 13's answer implies about the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the ברייתא as being about open barrels
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Open barrels are an אבידה מדעת, so the ברייתא's ruling would be too obvious to need teaching.

steps.title: Covered but not sealed
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא answers that the ברייתא is about barrels that are covered with a lid but not sealed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא said: the ברייתא is about barrels that are covered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a middle case for the ברייתא, so it is neither open nor sealed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A covered barrel is not an אבידה מדעת, because the wine is protected. But a lid alone has no seal that identifies the owner. So the finder keeps it because there is no סימן, not because the owner gave it up.

keyTerms.meaning: Covers it with a lid without sealing it

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya said: when he covers it.
phrases.notes: He means the lid is on, but there is no seal identifying the owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the ברייתא is not about sealed barrels, it must be about open ones.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about covered but unsealed barrels: they are not given up, but they have no identifying סימן.

steps.title: Both are sealed; the difference is timing
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a different answer. Both the משנה and the ברייתא are about sealed containers. The משנה is about before the wine storehouses open, and the ברייתא is about after they open.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: you can even say both are about sealed containers, and there is no contradiction. Here it is before the storehouses opened, and there it is after the storehouses opened.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a second way to resolve the contradiction from step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the storehouses open, few sealed barrels are around, so a seal points to a specific owner. After the storehouses open and sell to many people, lots of barrels carry the same seal. Then the seal no longer identifies anyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one
It is not difficult; there is no contradiction

phrases.english: Abaye said:
You can even say that both are about sealed containers
and it is not difficult:
here, it is before the storehouses were opened
phrases.notes: "Here" is the משנה, which requires an announcement.

phrases.english: there, it is after the storehouses were opened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the contradiction in step 12 and answers it differently from steps 13-15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference between the sources must be sealed vs. unsealed.
steps.terutzMaskana: A seal is a סימן only before the storehouses open. After that, many barrels share the same seal.

steps.title: אביי tells רב יעקב בר אבא to keep the barrel
steps.stepSummary: רב יעקב בר אבא found a barrel of wine after the storehouses opened. אביי told him to keep it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the case where רב יעקב בר אבא found a barrel of wine after the storehouses opened. He came before אביי, who said to him: go take it for yourself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up אביי's answer with a real case where he ruled this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows that אביי's split was a working rule, not just a theory. A barrel found after the storehouses opened has no useful סימן, so the finder keeps it.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרַב יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Like that case where Rav Ya'akov bar Abba
found a barrel of wine
after the storehouses were opened.
He came before Abaye,
and he said to him: Go take it for yourself.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַב יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's answer from step 16 with a case he decided.
steps.whatToRemember: Two answers to the barrels vs. jugs contradiction. First answer: רבי זירא in the name of רב says the משנה means sealed jugs, and רב הושעיא adds that the ברייתא means barrels that are covered but not sealed. Second answer: אביי says both are sealed, and a seal identifies the owner only before the storehouses open.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's rule that after the storehouses open, a sealed barrel goes to the finder
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב יעקב בר אבא and the barrel he found

steps.title: Is the place where something was found a סימן?
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי asks רב נחמן whether the location of a lost object counts as a סימן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי asked רב נחמן: is location a סימן, or is it not a סימן?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts: can an owner win back his item by saying exactly where he lost it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the סימנים were features of the item itself, like a seal or the shape of a cut. Now the question is whether something outside the item, its location, can also identify the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a real question of law)
Location, the place where the item was found
An identifying mark that lets an owner claim a lost item

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב בִּיבִי מֵרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Beivai asked Rav Nachman:
Is location a סימן
or is it not a סימן?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב בִּיבִי מֵרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question, separate from the barrels discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the place where an item was found can serve as a סימן

steps.title: The barrels ברייתא shows location is not a סימן
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers from the barrels ברייתא. If location were a סימן, the finder would have to announce the barrels and let the owner identify them by their location.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: you learned it already. One who finds barrels of wine, oil, grain, dried figs, or olives keeps them. And if you think location is a סימן, let him announce them, and the location will serve as the sign!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the question with a proof from the ברייתא quoted in step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every lost item was found in some place. If the place counted as a סימן, the finder of the barrels would have to announce them, and the owner could claim them by naming where they were. Since the ברייתא lets the finder keep them, location must not be a סימן.

keyTerms.meaning: You have learned it (it is already taught in a source)
And if it enters your mind; if you were to think

phrases.english: He said to him: You have learned it:

phrases.aramaic: מָצָא חָבִיּוֹת שֶׁל יַיִן וְשֶׁל שֶׁמֶן
phrases.english: One who found barrels of wine or of oil

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל תְּבוּאָה וְשֶׁל גְּרוֹגְרוֹת וְשֶׁל זֵיתִים
phrases.english: or of grain, or of dried figs, or of olives
these belong to him.
And if it enters your mind
that location is a סימן,
let him announce, with the location as the sign!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ דְּמָקוֹם הָוֵי סִימָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18 using the ברייתא from step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Location is not a סימן, as the barrels ברייתא shows.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about a riverbank
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד rejects the proof. The ברייתא is about barrels found on a riverbank, where location cannot identify anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: what are we dealing with here? With a riverbank.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב נחמן's proof by limiting the ברייתא to one special place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A riverbank is where ships unload goods belonging to many people. In that one place, location tells you nothing about the owner. So the ברייתא does not prove that location is never a סימן.

keyTerms.meaning: What are we dealing with here? (introduces a narrower case)

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said:
With what are we dealing here?
With the bank of a river.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב נחמן's proof from step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof only, not necessarily רב נחמן's conclusion
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may be about a riverbank, a crowded place where location identifies no one, so it says nothing about other places.

steps.title: Why a riverbank is not a סימן
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי explains that a riverbank is not a סימן because just as the owner happened to lose something there, someone else could have too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: why did רבנן say a riverbank is not a סימן? Because we tell the claimant: just as it happened to you, it also happened to someone else.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי explains the reason behind רב זביד's riverbank case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סימן only works if it points to one person. At a riverbank, many people's goods are put down, so naming that spot does not prove the item is yours.

phrases.english: Rav Mari said:
What is the reason that the Rabbis said
that a riverbank is not a סימן?
Because we say to him:
Just as it happened to you
it also happened to your fellow.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא אֲמַרוּ רַבָּנַן רַקְּתָא דְנַהֲרָא לָא הָוֵי סִימָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A riverbank is not a סימן because many people could have lost things in that same spot.

steps.title: Another version: no place is a סימן
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רב מרי applies the same reason to every location: anyone else could have put something in that same place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רב מרי said: why did רבנן say location is not a סימן? Because we tell the claimant: just as this place happened for you, this place also happened for someone else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב מרי's words that is much broader than the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, only a crowded spot like a riverbank fails to identify the owner. In this version, any place fails, because another person could just as easily have left something there. This version matches רב נחמן's view that location is not a סימן.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say; there is another version

phrases.english: Some say that Rav Mari said:
What is the reason that the Rabbis said
that location is not a סימן?
Because we say to him:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּאִתְרְמִי לְדִידָךְ הַאי מְקוֹם
phrases.english: Just as this place happened for you
this place also happened for your fellow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a broader version of רב מרי's statement from step 21.
steps.confusionAlert: The two versions of רב מרי use almost the same words but differ in scope. The first is only about a riverbank. The second is about any location at all.
steps.whatToRemember: Is location a סימן? רב נחמן proves from the barrels ברייתא that it is not. רב זביד limits that ברייתא to a riverbank. רב מרי's first version explains the riverbank case. His second version says no location is a סימן, because someone else could have left something in that same place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Location in general is not a סימן, since another person could equally have placed something in that same spot.

steps.title: The man who found pitch near the winepress
steps.stepSummary: A man found pitch near a winepress and asked רב what to do. רב told him to keep it, and when the man hesitated, רב told him to share it with רב's son חייא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man found pitch by a winepress. He came before רב, who told him: Go take it for yourself. רב saw that he was hesitating, so he told him: Go share some of it with my son חייא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a found object. It is setting up the next step, where the גמרא will try to learn from this story whether location counts as a סימן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pitch was found in a specific place, near a winepress, so the owner could in theory have identified it by its location. רב still let the finder keep it. When the man worried that this might be stealing, רב told him to share it with his own son to show that keeping it was fully allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Pitch, a sticky tar used to seal barrels and vessels

phrases.english: A certain man who found
pitch by the winepress,
came before Rav.
He said to him: Go take it for yourself.
He saw that he was hesitating,
so he said to him: Go share it
from it with Chiyya my son.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּאַשְׁכַּח כּוּפְרָא בֵּי מַעֲצַרְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new case that bears on רב ביבי's question of whether location is a סימן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב allowed the finder to keep pitch found near a winepress.

steps.title: Suggestion that רב holds location is not a sign
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב let the man keep the pitch because he holds that location does not count as a סימן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב holds that a location is not a סימן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove from the story that רב holds location is not a סימן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If location were a סימן, the owner could say 'I lost pitch by the winepress,' and the finder would have to announce it. Since רב let him keep it, it seems רב did not consider the place a way to identify the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? The גמרא's way of suggesting a conclusion that may be rejected
Location, the place where the item was found
An identifying mark the owner can describe to prove the item is his

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rav holds
that location is not a sign?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא קָא סָבַר רַב מָקוֹם לָא הָוֵי סִימָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a suggested inference from the story of רב.
steps.raayaObject: That location is not a סימן
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling in the pitch story

steps.title: The real reason was the owner's despair
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא rejects the proof. רב let the man keep the pitch because the owner had already given up on it, as shown by the grass growing through it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: The reason was יאוש בעלים, because רב saw that grass had grown up through the pitch.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא pushes back on the proof. The story has nothing to do with whether location is a סימן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grass growing through the pitch shows it had been lying there a long time. The owner surely gave up hope of getting it back, and once there is יאוש the finder may keep it even if it had a סימן. So the story cannot teach us anything about location.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner giving up hope of getting his lost item back

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אבא does not say location IS a סימן. He only says this story does not decide the question either way.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
It was because of the owner's despair that they dealt with it this way,
for he saw that grass was sprouting through it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: מִשּׁוּם יֵאוּשׁ בְּעָלִים נָגְעוּ בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 24.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the pitch story
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling is explained by יאוש בעלים, not by location failing to be a סימן.
steps.whyThisMatters: The question of whether location is a סימן stays open; this story cannot settle it.

steps.title: What are אנפוריא vessels?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the next line of the משנה, where רבי שמעון בן אלעזר speaks about אנפוריא vessels, and asks what that word means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says, and so on. What is אנפוריא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה and asking for the meaning of a hard word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a finder does not need to announce אנפוריא vessels. Before we can understand that rule, we need to know what kind of vessels these are.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of vessels mentioned in the משנה; its meaning is explained in the next step

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says, etc.
What is anpurya?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר וְכוּ׳. מַאי אַנְפּוּרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the location discussion to the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word אנפוריא

steps.title: New vessels the owner has not looked at enough
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that אנפוריא are new vessels that the owner has not yet looked at enough to know them well.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: They are new vessels that the eye has not yet had its fill of.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question and defines the word אנפוריא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the vessels are new, the owner has not had time to get familiar with how they look. That is why the משנה treats them differently from other found items.

keyTerms.meaning: The eye has had its fill of them, meaning the owner has looked at them enough to know them

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
New vessels
that the eye has not yet had its fill of.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כֵּלִים חֲדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אנפוריא are new vessels the owner has not looked at enough.

steps.title: Why should looking at them matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what difference it makes whether the owner looked at the vessels enough. If they have a סימן, he can describe it anyway. If they have no סימן, looking at them does not help.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If they have a סימן, why does it matter that the owner has not looked at them enough? If they have no סימן, why would it matter if he had looked at them enough?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's explanation by asking how being 'not looked at enough' could change the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules of lost objects depend on a סימן. With a סימן, even a quick look is enough for the owner to describe it. Without a סימן, the owner cannot prove ownership no matter how well he knows it, so his familiarity seems to make no difference.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How exactly are we picturing it?
What of it? What difference does it make?

phrases.english: What is the case?
If they have a sign,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לֹא שְׂבָעָתַן הָעַיִן מַאי הָוֵי?
phrases.english: what difference does it make that the eye has not had its fill of them?
If they have no sign,
what difference would it make if the eye had its fill of them?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי אִית בְּהוּ סִימָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the definition given in step 27.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Either way, with or without a סימן, the owner's familiarity with the vessels seems to make no legal difference.

steps.title: It matters for a Torah scholar who recognizes by sight
steps.stepSummary: The vessels really have no סימן. The difference is for a צורבא מרבנן, whom we trust to recognize his item by sight. If he looked at it enough, we return it; if not, we do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, they have no סימן. The difference is about returning an item to a צורבא מרבנן based on טביעות עין. If he has looked at them enough, he is sure of them and we return it. If he has not looked at them enough, he is not sure of them and we do not return it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by finding a case where familiarity does matter: a Torah scholar who claims to recognize the item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an item with no סימן is not returned. A צורבא מרבנן is an exception, because we trust him when he says he recognizes it by sight. With new vessels he has not looked at enough, he cannot truly recognize them, so even he does not get them back.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually; it introduces the answer that keeps one of the options
Recognizing something by sight, without a specific mark

steps.whatToRemember: An item without a סימן can still be returned to a צורבא מרבנן who recognizes it by sight, but only if he has looked at it enough to really know it.

phrases.english: Really, it is where they have no sign,
and the difference is for returning it
to a Torah scholar based on recognition by sight.
If the eye has had its fill of them, he is certain about them,
and we return it to him.
When the eye has not had its fill of them,
he is not certain about them,
and we do not return it to him,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a special case where the distinction matters
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a סימן, familiarity with the item never helps anyone get it back.
steps.terutzMaskana: Familiarity matters for a צורבא מרבנן, who can reclaim an item by טביעות עין, but only if he has looked at it enough.

steps.title: Why a Torah scholar is trusted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports trusting a צורבא מרבנן with a teaching of שמואל: Torah scholars change their words only in three matters, such as a tractate and a bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: In these three matters only, Torah scholars are used to changing their words: about a tractate, and about a bed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source that explains why we can believe a Torah scholar who says he recognizes the item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A צורבא מרבנן does not bend the truth except in a few special cases, like saying out of modesty that he did not learn a tractate. A lost-object claim is not one of these cases, so his word that he recognizes the item can be trusted.

keyTerms.meaning: Change their words, say something not exactly true

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
In these three matters
Torah scholars are used to changing their words:
about a tractate, and about a bed
phrases.notes: Only two of the three are listed here; the third comes right after this.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: בְּהָנֵי תְּלָת מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 29 by explaining why a scholar's claim is believed.
steps.raayaObject: That a צורבא מרבנן is trusted when he claims טביעות עין
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's teaching that scholars change their words only in three matters
